findings.native_candidate: Heat, at 100m2 solar collector in PVT system, Al-Cu, slanted roof, hot water heat storage
findings.finding: Native PVT hot-water output is not an established substitute for industrial/district CSP heat. Its paired electricity allocation and excluded auxiliary heating require explicit grade and system-boundary review. Borehole regeneration output is also not delivered useful heat. Combined solar+wood/gas outputs cannot represent pure solar supply without double-counting fossil/wood generation.
findings.decision: Do not accept these native candidates as industrial CSP aliases. Inspect the dedicated published CLIC heat CSP root and its complete dependencies next; do not reuse the electricity output per MJ.

heat, industrial, from hydrogen fuel cell
findings.native_candidate: Heat, residential, by conversion of hydrogen using fuel cell, SOFC, allocated by exergy, distributed by pipeline, produced by Electrolysis, PEM using electricity from grid
findings.finding: Native SOFC documentation states 33% heat conversion and 8% exergy allocation. Allocated inventory fuel draw cannot be inverted to infer physical conversion. Existing IAM source proxy is PEM, introducing an explicit technology difference.
findings.decision: Retain complete allocated inventory if accepted, but derive nominal final-energy conversion from independently documented physical performance. Add an explicit reviewed allocated-conversion path with quantity witnesses and refusal tests before admitting these roles. No deallocation, additional electricity credit or inferred efficiency.

findings.native_candidate: Heat, hard coal coke, at stove 5-15kW
findings.finding: Same-fuel native candidate is a small historical German stove, not industrial secondary heat. The current ecoinvent role explicitly uses the industrial hard-coal furnace as a proxy.
findings.decision: Compare full native industrial hard-coal proxy with small coke stove before choosing. Retain fuel/technology/geography warnings; do not silently substitute same-fuel name alone.

findings.finding: Found native ground/water source heat pumps, not an established dedicated deep-geothermal heat plant counterpart. Pump output and borehole-regeneration services have different energy boundaries.
findings.decision: Inspect the retained deep-geothermal workbook family and physical heat reference. Do not map geothermal heat to ambient extraction or another heat-pump role by name.

CCS_next_step: Inspect complete heat co-product source roots and their allocations, capture energy demand and storage chain. Electricity CCS approval alone does not establish heat allocation or justify extra capture/storage burdens.
residual_next_step: Review a frozen native delivered-heat composition separately from IAM-updated markets, to avoid cycles, duplicated supply and invented residual fuel shares.
